title: Civil War
subtitle: Registration divides the heroes
intro: The 2006 comic event, not the film, Civil War II, or 2015’s Battleworld Civil War: Warzones. The seven-issue main series gives the complete central conflict. Setup and side books are optional; the side-track order lists repeat core issues as anchors, not additional books to read twice. This is a selective library path rather than every tie-in. Published dates and story-placement order can differ.

steps.title: The Road to Civil War
steps.issues: Amazing Spider-Man (1999) #529–531; Fantastic Four (1998) #536–537; New Avengers: Illuminati (2006) one-shot
steps.why: Political background before the Stamford crisis. Useful context, not a prerequisite.
steps.match: The Road to Civil War contains these setup stories. The Illuminati one-shot is not the later five-issue Illuminati miniseries.

steps.title: Civil War — the complete main series
steps.why: Read all seven issues in numbered order; this is the central event.
steps.match: Choose either edition: both collect #1–7. Warzones, House of M: Civil War, and the movie prelude do not replace this story.

steps.title: Optional Spider-Man track
steps.why: Peter’s decisions and personal cost. Use this selective interleave if you want his side alongside the core.
steps.match: Civil War: Amazing Spider-Man collects #532–538. The separate Peter Parker, Spider-Man volume collects Sensational Spider-Man, a different parallel branch.

steps.title: Optional civilian viewpoint: Front Line
steps.why: Reporters follow the conflict beyond the headline battles. Its final issue belongs after the main finale.
steps.match: The Complete Collection covers #1–11. The two smaller Front Line volumes overlap it. This side book is not needed to finish the core.
order: Civil War: Front Line #1–10 — parallel to Civil War #1–7; read after the core as a companion if avoiding switches
Civil War #7 must precede Civil War: Front Line #11

steps.title: Captain America #25: immediate fallout
steps.why: The major Captain America consequence comes after the event’s finale.
steps.match: The Death of the Dream contains #25–30. Read #25 here; #26–30 continue Cap’s own series after these immediate epilogues.

steps.title: The Confession
steps.why: A focused epilogue for Tony and Steve. Read after Captain America #25.
steps.match: Civil War: Iron Man includes The Confession plus Iron Man #13–14 and Casualties of War. This step uses only The Confession; the other contents belong earlier.

steps.title: Fallen Son: The Death of Captain America
steps.issues: Fallen Son: The Death of Captain America #1–5
steps.why: Five reactions to the loss explored in Captain America #25.
steps.match: No confirmed collection match in the supplied catalog. The Death of Captain America collections are Brubaker’s ongoing story, not this separate miniseries.
